resolved.title: Peopleware: Productive Projects and Teams
resolved.author: Tom DeMarco; Tim Lister
resolved.reason: English explanation of the human constraints on software production. Management advice accompanies an account of work environments and team behavior; it is not a technical training course. No serious veto established. Consultant experience and selected examples support heuristics more strongly than universal causal claims.

resolved.title: Enterprise Architecture as Strategy
resolved.author: Jeanne W. Ross; Peter Weill; David C. Robertson
resolved.reason: English systems account of operating models and shared digital infrastructure. Borderline H3: implementation advice is substantial, but the explanatory value of integration, standardization and local/global tradeoffs can be obtained without professional architecture training. Retain with moderate eligibility confidence. No serious veto established.

resolved.title: Coders at Work: Reflections on the Craft of Programming
resolved.author: Peter Seibel
resolved.reason: English interviews and intellectual biographies, not a course or technical reference. The science/high-tech biography exception also protects it from a personality-only V3 judgment. Correct the intake description: the published contents contain fifteen interviews, not sixteen. No serious veto established.

resolved.title: The Cathedral and the Bazaar
resolved.author: Eric S. Raymond
resolved.reason: A published English essay collection, despite the title essay circulating online first. The book began in 1999; the 1997 essay is not used as the book publication year. Explanatory software-organization analysis, not a programming manual. Advocacy alone does not establish V2 or V5. Selected successful cases constrain generalization.

resolved.title: Everybody Lies
resolved.author: Seth Stephens-Davidowitz
resolved.reason: English explanatory account of behavioral data, not a data-science curriculum. No serious veto established from the inspected evidence. Searches are imperfect proxies; causal interpretations need more caution than demonstrations of concealed behavior. T11 applies to the predominantly American social examples; the core method is data analysis, so T12=0.

resolved.title: Future Shock
resolved.author: Alvin Toffler
resolved.reason: English cross-domain argument about accelerating change, not a technical curriculum. Read as dated speculation rather than current scientific findings. No serious veto established at this evidence level. H13=0: a broad forward-looking argument has no single historical endpoint; its age is charged under P14.

resolved.title: Here Comes Everybody
resolved.author: Clay Shirky
resolved.reason: English explanation of digitally enabled collective action; no technical curriculum. No serious veto established. The optimistic treatment of coordination needs qualification by institutional limits. T12=-10 because media-enabled social organization, not technical construction, is central. Broad mechanism account: no H13 endpoint.

resolved.title: The Shallows: What the Internet Is Doing to Our Brains
resolved.author: Nicholas Carr
resolved.reason: English analysis of media and cognition, not training. No serious veto established from the inspected material. Generalizing from cognitive experiments to lasting internet effects needs caution. Media is central: T12 applies. It is not chiefly a disease account, so T11=0.

resolved.title: The Art of Intrusion
resolved.author: Kevin D. Mitnick; William L. Simon
resolved.reason: English accounts of actual intrusions, distinct from the fictionalized cases in The Art of Deception. Main purpose is explanatory case narrative; prevention summaries do not make it a procedural training course. No serious veto established. Anonymous participants and retrospective accounts constrain reliability.

resolved.title: The Industries of the Future
resolved.author: Alec Ross
resolved.reason: English survey of technological change and economic development, not a training manual. No serious veto established from the inspected publisher excerpt. Forecasting deserves a durability discount; it is not automatically V4. Technology remains central despite policy and finance applications. Forward-looking scope: H13=0.
